title: Supergene chalcocite enrichment blanket over porphyry copper deposits
percentile_convention: USGS: p90 is the value that 90% of deposits equal or exceed (the small end); p10 the large end

sources.citation: John, D.A., Ayuso, R.A., Barton, M.D., Blakely, R.J., Bodnar, R.J., Dilles, J.H., Gray, Floyd, Graybeal, F.T., Mars, J.C., McPhee, D.K., Seal, R.R., Taylor, R.D., and Vikre, P.G., 2010, Porphyry copper deposit model, chap. B of Mineral deposit models for resource assessment: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2010-5070-B, 169 p.
Singer, D.A., Berger, V.I., and Moring, B.C., 2008, Porphyry copper deposits of the world: database and grade and tonnage models, 2008: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2008-1155, 45 p.
Singer, D.A., Berger, V.I., and Moring, B.C., 2008, companion data file PorCuTX2008.txt of U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2008-1155 ('Comments' field).

Sillitoe, R.H., and McKee, E.H., 1996, Age of supergene oxidation and enrichment in the Chilean porphyry copper province: Economic Geology, v. 91, no. 1, p. 164-179, doi:10.2113/gsecongeo.91.1.164. Abstract as published on the USGS Publications Warehouse (record 70018070; E.H. McKee, USGS).
sources.licence: Abstract text on a USGS (public-domain) web page; the full article is published by the Society of Economic Geologists. Only facts (numbers) are taken from it.

sources.citation: Not a publication. Marks a value supplied by the digitiser where the USGS text gives only a verbal range; the entry's note says what the value is based on.

tonnage_mt.note: USGS publishes no grade-tonnage model for supergene blankets. OFR 2008-1155 does not separate them: 'Deposits that may be derived from, or affected by, hypogene and supergene processes are included in the models' (OFR 2008-1155, PDF p. 4), so the porphyry_cu tonnages include supergene ore. SIR 2010-5070-B gives only ranges: enriched copper sulfide ore 'tens of megatons to more than 1.5 gigatons' (see extra enriched_sulfide_tonnage_mt_*).

cu_pct.note: No percentiles published. Range for enriched copper sulfide ore: 0.4 to 1.7 percent Cu (extra enriched_sulfide_cu_pct_min/max); 'Enriched copper sulfide ores are invariably higher grade than underlying hypogene ore or copper-mineralized rock'. Mo, Au, Ag: 'Enrichment of molybdenum, gold, and silver in PCDs by weathering and enrichment processes has not been documented' (p. 65, PDF p. 79); 'There are no published data that distinguish hypogene and supergene grades of silver and gold' (p. 4, PDF p. 18).

ore_density_t_m3.where: p. 4 (PDF p. 18); whole report text searched for density, specific gravity, t/m3 and g/cm3 with no numeric value found
ore_density_t_m3.note: No numeric density. Qualitative only: 'Many gangue minerals formed by hypogene and supergene processes have lower densities than the primary rock-forming minerals and hypogene hydrothermal minerals they replace. Lower density gangue minerals, combined with voids created by mineral dissolution, generally decrease physical competency of ore and waste' (p. 4). Leached capping is 'porous and partly decomposed iron oxide-rich rock' (p. 120, PDF p. 134).

deposits_per_1e5_km2.note: Not applicable as a free-standing density: blankets sit on porphyry Cu deposits (use porphyry_cu). No USGS source opened gives the fraction of porphyry deposits that carry a blanket; SIR 2010-5070-B p. 66 (PDF p. 80) notes only that supergene copper minerals are reported from fewer deposits than hypogene ones, 'reflecting maturity of operating mines and infrequent discovery of enriched deposits'.

min_separation_m.note: Not applicable: the blanket is part of its host porphyry deposit, which follows the 2-km rule in porphyry_cu.

enrichment_factor_andes_max.where: Section J 'Formation and Distribution', p. 66 (PDF p. 80)
enrichment_factor_andes_max.note: 'Copper grades of enriched copper sulfide zones are up to 3 times those of underlying hypogene ore or copper-mineralized rock in Andean PCDs (Sillitoe, 2005).' USGS restatement of Sillitoe (2005). Applies to Cu only.

enrichment_factor_sw_north_america_max.where: p. 66 (PDF p. 80); also section R, p. 120 (PDF p. 134)
enrichment_factor_sw_north_america_max.note: p. 66: 'Enrichment factors in some southwestern North American PCDs approach 8' (Titley and Marozas, 1995). p. 120: blanket-like zones of chalcocite 'with up to 8 times the grades of the original hypogene mineralization'.

hypogene_cu_pct_sw_north_america_min.note: 'based on hypogene ore grades of 0.07 to 0.6 percent copper and enrichment ore grades 0.34 to 1.12 percent copper' (Titley and Marozas, 1995).

enriched_cu_pct_sw_north_america_min.note: Enrichment-ore grades in the same southwestern North American deposits.

pyrite_to_cu_sulfide_ratio_optimal.note: 'Enriched copper sulfide ore is best developed above hypogene ore or copper-mineralized rocks that contain about 5 times as much pyrite as copper sulfide minerals.' Pyrite/chalcopyrite in the southwestern North American examples 'varies from about 3 to more than 10'. Leaching needs enough pyrite to make acid (p. 120, PDF p. 134).

enriched_sulfide_cu_pct_min.note: Enriched copper sulfide ore zones consist of tonnages 'at 0.4 to 1.7 percent copper'.

enriched_sulfide_tonnage_mt_min.where: based on sir2010-5070B p. 4 (PDF p. 18) and p. 65 (PDF p. 79)
enriched_sulfide_tonnage_mt_min.note: PLACEHOLDER, NOT A USGS NUMBER: the text says 'tens of megatons to more than 1.5 gigatons'; 10 Mt is the smallest value the phrase 'tens of megatons' allows.

enriched_sulfide_tonnage_mt_max.note: 'more than 1.5 gigatons': the largest enriched sulfide ore zones exceed this, so it is a lower bound on the maximum.

enriched_zone_thickness_m_typical_max.where: 'Vertical Extent', p. 25 (PDF p. 39); section L, p. 67 (PDF p. 81)
enriched_zone_thickness_m_typical_max.note: p. 25: the vertical extent of supergene enriched copper ore 'varies considerably ... but seldom exceeds 200 m'. p. 67: 'Supergene-enriched zones can range from a few meters to more than 200 meters in thickness'. p. 4: enriched copper sulfide ore zones 'are mostly tens to several hundred meters thick'.

enriched_zone_thickness_m_max.note: 'Enriched copper sulfide ores are as much as 750 m thick but most are tens to several hundred meters thick'.

leached_cap_thickness_m_min.note: 'The thickness of leached capping is highly variable and ranges from 0 to several hundred meters in most PCDs.'

leached_cap_thickness_m_max.where: based on sir2010-5070B p. 4 (PDF p. 18), p. 65 (PDF p. 79) and p. 67 (PDF p. 81)
leached_cap_thickness_m_max.note: PLACEHOLDER, NOT A USGS NUMBER: 300 m is the smallest reading of 'several hundred meters'. Note that p. 67 says supergene-enriched zones 'generally have a hematitic leached cap as much as tens of meters in thickness', so tens of metres is the usual case and hundreds the extreme.

oxide_zone_thickness_m_max.note: Supergene copper oxide ore zones 'are as much as 300 m thick, but more commonly tens to less than 200 m thick, and consist of tens to several hundred megatons'. Most non-exotic oxide ore lies immediately above the enriched sulfide zone (p. 66).

oxide_ore_cu_pct_min.note: 'at 0.34 to 1+ percent copper' (the summary on p. 4, PDF p. 18, rounds to '0.3 to greater than 1 percent'). Oxide ore grades are 'both lower and higher than grades of hypogene sources'.

exotic_oxide_cu_pct_min.note: Exotic oxide ore zones: 'tens to several hundred megatons at 0.27 to 1+ percent copper' (p. 4 summary says 0.3). Copper can move laterally 'hundreds or thousands of meters from its initial hypogene position' (p. 121, PDF p. 135); position controlled by the pyrite halo and the paleowater table (Fig. J1 caption, p. 65).

blanket_position_water_table.where: section R, p. 120 (PDF p. 134); section L, p. 67 (PDF p. 81)
blanket_position_water_table.note: p. 120: blankets 'are considered to have formed at the top of the water table because their upper boundaries are generally planar and parallel to the present surface or to a paleosurface. The lower boundaries of enrichment blankets are more diffuse and marked by a gradual decrease in chalcocite abundance and copper grade and increase in unenriched chalcopyrite with depth.' p. 67: metals are redeposited 'in more reducing, higher pH areas, that is, below the water table'; profile is leached zone (gossan) over supergene zone over hypogene ore. Leaching needs the rate of leaching and water-table drawdown to exceed the erosion rate (p. 120). Depth to the blanket top therefore equals the leached-cap (+ oxide-zone) thickness.

zoning_chalcocite_over_covellite.note: 'Chalcocite (Cu2S) precipitates on top where Cu+2/HS- is high; covellite (CuS) precipitates below chalcocite where Cu+2/HS- is lower.' Copper in enriched sulfide ore is mostly chalcocite, lesser covellite and CuxSy minerals (p. 66). Partial replacement of pyrite/chalcopyrite at the base of the zone, complete replacement of pyrite by chalcocite in mature upper parts (p. 66).

supergene_duration_per_deposit_myr_min.where: USGS Publications Warehouse record 70018070, abstract ('Supergene activity at individual deposits lasted for at least 0.4 to 6.2 m.y.')
supergene_duration_per_deposit_myr_min.note: Northern Chile, 25 supergene alunite K/Ar ages. These are MINIMUM durations of supergene activity per deposit. The research note's 'typically 3-9 Myr' (attributed to Sillitoe, 2005) was not found in any USGS document opened; SIR 2010-5070-B defers rates to Sillitoe (2005) (p. 68, PDF p. 82).

supergene_duration_per_deposit_myr_max.note: Upper end of the minimum-duration range. Example outside Chile: the OFR 2008-1155 data file (Comments field of Tyrone, New Mexico; source ofr2008-1155-data) records 'Two stages of supergene enrichment 19.2-16.2 Ma and 8.7-4.6 Ma'.

supergene_onset_lag_myr_min.where: Abstract ('Supergene activity commenced no less than 11 m.y. after generation of each porphyry copper deposit because of the time required to unroof the copper-bearing parts of the system')
supergene_onset_lag_myr_min.note: Northern Chile. Contrast: at El Salvador, Chile, SIR 2010-5070-B p. 68 (PDF p. 82) reports weathering beginning 'within 6 m.y. (about 36-35 Ma) from the end of hypogene mineralization at about 41 Ma' (Mote and others, 2001) - see supergene_onset_lag_el_salvador_myr.

supergene_onset_lag_el_salvador_myr.unit: Myr after end of hypogene mineralization
supergene_onset_lag_el_salvador_myr.note: 'weathering to have begun within 6 m.y. (about 36-35 Ma) from the end of hypogene mineralization at about 41 Ma. They identified multiple supergene events at 35 Ma, 25 Ma, 14 Ma, and 11 Ma' (Mote and others, 2001), i.e. repeated events over ~24 Myr.

supergene_province_active_span_myr_min.note: Supergene oxidation and enrichment in northern Chile were active from about 34 to 14 Ma, 'a minimum of 20 m.y.', and ceased at about 14 Ma with increasing aridity.

precipitation_cm_per_yr_min.where: Section L 'Effects of Hydrologic Setting', p. 68 (PDF p. 82)
precipitation_cm_per_yr_min.note: Central Andes, late Oligocene to middle Miocene maximum enrichment: 'Precipitation for this period, inferred to be 10 cm/year or more' (Clark and others, 1990). Semiarid climate plus episodic uplift; supergene enrichment also occurs from tropical to arid climates (Titley, 1978), and even in the hyperarid Atacama; the critical factor is permeability.
